scope: Read-only investigation of prior Windows runner failure and bounded diagnostic mitigation; no proof of native root cause.
runtime_observed: CPython 3.13.16 x64 Windows; workflow requests ordinary 3.13, not free-threaded build. Runtime GIL state was not captured.
observations: Two 120-second periodic C-level stack dumps completed and tests continued.
The third dump ended mid-line in statement_facts.py, followed by process exit code 1; no complete exception traceback or regression JSON was produced.
The last public-business test started about 11 seconds before the last periodic dump; this was not a 120-second per-test timeout.

Local search found no test explicitly closing stderr, dup2-ing its descriptor, calling os._exit, or reloading faulthandler before the failure. Temporary object mocks of sys.stderr exist but do not by themselves close the original stream.

primary_sources.finding: Timed dumps default to exit=False; only exit=True requests immediate exit(1). The output descriptor must remain open; descriptor replacement can redirect the dump.

The timer calls _Py_DumpTracebackThreads from its watchdog thread. Its exit flag defaults to zero. The manual Python dump path has a stop-the-world wrapper that is absent from this timer path; this is not a reproduction of the observed failure.
A primary report reproduces timer-dump use of freed code metadata on debug Linux main/3.16. It supports a related risk, not a Windows 3.13 root-cause claim.
Python-owned current-frame snapshots are intended for specialized deadlock diagnosis; active-thread frames are a snapshot rather than a stable statement of later activity.

mitigation: Replace periodic C-level timer sampling with a daemon Python watchdog using Event waits, sys._current_frames and traceback.format_stack; discard all frame references after each snapshot and before output I/O.
Keep the 120-second diagnostic interval and existing 45-minute CI test-step watchdog. Diagnostic snapshots are not test deadlines.

Atomically persist an initial running report, selected/discovered identities before execution, first-start progress, later progress at most every five seconds on test boundaries, and failure/error details immediately. Complete exact execution is required before status can be passed.
The collector is unchanged and rejects a running report or missing/duplicate executions. No skipped or interrupted test is converted into a pass.
limits: No Windows reproduction of the native failure has been established; this isolates a plausible diagnostic risk without declaring the public business test defective.
A Python watchdog cannot run while native code permanently holds the GIL; external CI timeout remains the finite backstop.
A hard process exit may leave only the last persisted checkpoint. START/END stdout retains finer-grained last activity where output flushing succeeded.
No native crash stack is guaranteed when the process terminates abruptly. No build, dispatch, cancellation, release, paid model or product change was performed by this subtask.
